**Method.** A divisor d is picked directly exactly when it comes before all of its proper multiples in a random ordering of the divisors. The reason is that d can only be erased by the pick of one of its multiples, and any multiple of a multiple of d is also a multiple of d. Among the set M(d) of multiples of d, each element is equally likely to come first, so P(d picked) = 1/|M(d)|. By linearity of expectation, the expected number of picks, which is the expected time, is the sum of these probabilities.

**Setup.** Here 1260 = 2²·3²·5·7, so 1260² = 2⁴·3⁴·5²·7². For d = 2^{a₁}3^{a₂}5^{a₃}7^{a₄}, we get |M(d)| = (5−a₁)(5−a₂)(3−a₃)(3−a₄). The sum factors into a product of one sum per prime.

- Each of the two sums for the primes 5 and 7 is H₃ = 11/6.
- So E = (137/60)²(11/6)² = (18769 · 121)/(3600 · 36) = 2271049/129600.
